advantage_archetypes.name: The well-connected inheritor
advantage_archetypes.description: Family wealth, parent domain expertise, and inherited professional networks. Multiple advantages stacking from birth — money, knowledge, and connections.

sample_trajectories.event: Founded Milo.com, a local product search engine indexing real-time store inventory, after dropping out of Wharton.
Sold Milo.com to eBay for approximately $75 million; became Head of Local at eBay.
Founded Atomic, a San Francisco-based startup studio and venture capital firm, with an initial $20 million fund.
Co-founded Hims & Hers Health, which became the second-fastest U.S. company to reach $1 billion valuation.
Atomic raised $260 million in additional funding; Hims & Hers went public via SPAC at a $1.6 billion valuation.
Co-founded HarvardConnection (later ConnectU), a social networking site at Harvard.
Filed lawsuit against Mark Zuckerberg alleging he stole their ConnectU idea to create Facebook.
Won gold medal in the eights and silver in the coxless four at the Pan American Games in Rio de Janeiro.
Competed in the men's pair rowing event at the Beijing Olympics, finishing 6th; received $65 million settlement from Facebook lawsuit.
Invested ~$11 million in Bitcoin, purchasing approximately 100,000 BTC.
Co-founded Gemini, a regulated US cryptocurrency exchange.
Filed for Gemini IPO on Nasdaq under symbol 'GEMI', with an estimated valuation of ~$2.1 billion.
Co-founded HarvardConnection (later ConnectU), a social networking site at Harvard, with brother Cameron and Divya Narendra.
Filed lawsuit against Mark Zuckerberg alleging he stole their ConnectU idea to create Facebook.
Won gold medal in the eights and silver in the coxless four at the Pan American Games in Rio de Janeiro.
Competed in the men's pair rowing event at the Beijing Olympics with Cameron, finishing 6th; received $65 million settlement from Facebook lawsuit.
Invested ~$11 million with Cameron in Bitcoin, purchasing approximately 100,000 BTC.
Co-founded Gemini, a regulated US cryptocurrency exchange, serving as CEO.
Filed for Gemini IPO on Nasdaq under symbol 'GEMI', with an estimated valuation of ~$2.1 billion.

advantage_archetypes.name: The domain heir
advantage_archetypes.description: Parents had expertise in the same field, paired with elite coaching and institutional access. Domain knowledge transferred from childhood, then compounded through dedicated mentorship and pipeline programs.

sample_trajectories.event: Released the Morris worm from MIT, the first Internet worm, infecting approximately 10% of internet-connected computers
First person convicted under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act; sentenced to 3 years probation, 400 hours community service, and $10,050 fine
Co-founded Viaweb with Paul Graham, one of the first software-as-a-service companies
Viaweb acquired by Yahoo for approximately $49 million in stock, rebranded as Yahoo Store
Co-founded Y Combinator with Paul Graham, Jessica Livingston, and Trevor Blackwell
Received tenure at MIT in the Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Elected to the National Academy of Engineering
Graduated from Cambridge with Addison-Wesley award for highest marks in computer science (93% average, highest in Cambridge CS history).
Co-founded Elixir Studios with Demis Hassabis as CTO and lead programmer, securing a three-game deal with Eidos Interactive.
Completed PhD at University of Alberta under Richard Sutton; co-developed MoGo, one of the strongest Go programs.
Led the team that developed AlphaGo, which defeated world Go champion Lee Sedol.
Awarded the ACM Prize in Computing for breakthrough advances in computer game-playing.
Named WHL Most Valuable Player and Canadian Hockey League Player of the Year after scoring 160 points for Swift Current Broncos; drafted 15th overall by Quebec Nordiques.
Made NHL debut on October 6, 1988, scoring 62 points in 70 games as a rookie with the Quebec Nordiques.
Finished ninth in the NHL with 102 points in the 1989-90 season, establishing himself as an elite NHL center.
Became sole captain of the Quebec Nordiques franchise.
Led the Colorado Avalanche to their first Stanley Cup championship, winning the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP with 34 points in 22 games.
Won the Hart Trophy as NHL MVP and led the Avalanche to a second Stanley Cup championship.
Retired from the NHL after 20 seasons with 1,641 career points.
Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame.

advantage_archetypes.name: The multiply-advantaged
advantage_archetypes.description: High advantage scores across several dimensions. Multiple compounding early advantages.

sample_trajectories.event: Co-created Phoenix (later Firefox) with Dave Hyatt; first public release Phoenix 0.1 on September 23, 2002.
Firefox 1.0 launched on November 9, 2004; downloaded 27 million+ times, challenging Internet Explorer's browser dominance.
Nominated for Wired magazine's Renegade of the Year award and included in Rolling Stone's 2005 hot list.
Co-founded Parakey, a web OS startup, with Joe Hewitt.
Parakey acquired by Facebook as its first acquisition; Ross joined Facebook as an engineer.
Left Facebook as Director of Product after six years to pursue new projects.
Purchased an $8.25 million condominium in Soho, New York City.
Graduated from the University of Washington with a degree in computer science.
Released Crypto++ 1.0, a free open-source C++ cryptographic library that became widely used in academia and industry.
Published the b-money proposal, an anonymous distributed electronic cash system that was cited as the first reference in the Bitcoin whitepaper.
Was one of the first two people contacted by Satoshi Nakamoto during Bitcoin's development.
Stepped away from the Crypto++ project, with the open-source community continuing maintenance.
Completed PhD in distributed systems at the University of Exeter, having spent most of his time on cryptography.
Invented Hashcash, a proof-of-work system for combating email spam, posted to the Cypherpunks mailing list.
Published the Hashcash white paper elaborating on the proof-of-work system.
Was one of the first two people contacted by Satoshi Nakamoto during Bitcoin's development.
Co-founded Blockstream, a Bitcoin infrastructure company focused on sidechains and layer-two scaling.
Blockstream raised $210 million in Series B financing, reaching a valuation of $3.2 billion and unicorn status.
Launched Bitcoin Standard Treasury Company (BSTR) in partnership with Cantor Fitzgerald to go public.

advantage_archetypes.name: The coached prodigy
advantage_archetypes.description: Identified early by an institutional pipeline, developed by dedicated coaches, and backed by a natural physical or talent edge. Common in sports and performance arts.

sample_trajectories.event: Began graduate studies at UC Berkeley, joining Bob Fabry's Computer Systems Research Group to work on BSD UNIX
1BSD released including his vi text editor and C shell, establishing him as the principal author of BSD UNIX
Completed MS in electrical engineering and computer science at Berkeley; 3BSD released with virtual memory support
Co-founded Sun Microsystems with Scott McNealy, Vinod Khosla, and Andy Bechtolsheim
Received the ACM Grace Murray Hopper Award for his contributions to operating systems and networking
Inspired the development of Java programming language at Sun Microsystems
Published influential essay 'Why The Future Doesn't Need Us' in Wired magazine
Left Sun Microsystems; later joined Kleiner Perkins as partner in 2005
Co-authored Lex with Mike Lesk at Bell Labs, creating the standard Unix lexical analyzer generator.
Joined Sun Microsystems as its first software manager, later rising to CTO.
Became CEO of Novell, a networking software company.
Became CEO of Google, guiding its transformation from startup to global tech giant.
Transitioned to Executive Chairman of Google (and later Alphabet), stepping down as CEO.
Founded Schmidt Futures, a philanthropic initiative investing in AI and scientific talent.
Won silver medal at the International Chemistry Olympiad and became first North Dakota finalist in Intel Science Talent Search since 1973.
Dropped out of MIT to join Stripe as a founding engineer (employee #4-5).
Became Stripe's first CTO, scaling the company from 5 to over 200 employees.
Left Stripe and co-founded OpenAI with Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever, and others.
Serves as President of OpenAI, one of the world's leading AI companies valued at over $150 billion.

advantage_archetypes.name: The adversity-forged striver
advantage_archetypes.description: Early hardship acted as a catalyst. Low inherited advantage, but adversity created drive and resilience that compensated.

sample_trajectories.event: Became a VJ for MTV, hosting Headbangers Ball and MTV Top 20 Video Countdown.
Registered mtv.com, one of the first celebrity-managed domain names, launching his internet career.
Co-founded Think New Ideas Inc., which IPO'd on NASDAQ during the dot-com bubble.
Co-founded PodShow (later Mevio), helping pioneer the podcasting medium.
Launched the No Agenda podcast with John C. Dvorak, which became a long-running independent podcast.
Co-founded Podcast Index, a decentralized podcast directory preserving open RSS-based podcasting.
Co-founded Etsy in a Brooklyn apartment with Chris Maguire and Haim Schoppik, launching the online crafts marketplace.
Stepped down as Etsy CEO, replaced by Maria Thomas.
Resumed role as Etsy CEO from December 2009.
Forced out of Etsy; company had revenues over $40 million.
Opened Catskill Mill, a community workshop for artisans in former downtown Catskill buildings.
Etsy went public via IPO, raising $237 million at $1.8 billion valuation.
Working on Dopple Works, a stealth handheld AR/XR device company.
Founded Silicon Alley Reporter, a newsletter that grew into a 300-page magazine covering New York's tech scene.
Co-founded Weblogs, Inc. with Brian Alvey, a blog network backed by Mark Cuban's angel investment.
Sold Weblogs, Inc. to AOL for approximately $25-30 million.
Launched Mahalo, a web directory that raised $20M in venture capital.
Made $25K angel investment in Uber through Sequoia Capital's scout program, later returning ~$100M.
Launched This Week in Startups podcast and the LAUNCH accelerator.
Became co-host of the All-In podcast, one of the most popular tech/business podcasts.

advantage_archetypes.name: The cofounder-paired builder
advantage_archetypes.description: Found exceptional cofounders or peers early, with direct customer exposure. Advantage came from people and partnerships, not family wealth or domain inheritance.

sample_trajectories.event: Co-founded Odeo, a podcasting company, with Evan Williams after his AudBlog startup merged with Williams' operation.
Co-founded Twitter within Odeo; coined the name 'Twitter' and helped design core features.
Ousted from Twitter by Evan Williams, who acquired Odeo's assets and renamed it Obvious Corporation.
Co-authored the seminal Goldwasser-Micali paper on probabilistic encryption at STOC, introducing semantic security to cryptography.
Completed PhD at UC Berkeley under Manuel Blum with thesis 'Probabilistic Encryption: Theory and Applications.'
Co-authored the foundational paper on zero-knowledge proofs with Micali and Rackoff.
Awarded the Godel Prize for work on interactive proofs.
Received the Grace Murray Hopper Award.
Won the ACM Turing Award jointly with Silvio Micali for foundational contributions to cryptography.
Became director of the Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing at UC Berkeley, serving until 2024.
Dropped out of University of Cincinnati and moved to San Francisco to work as a web developer at CNET on GameSpot and other sites.
Co-founded GitHub with Tom Preston-Werner and PJ Hyett; public launch in April 2008, reaching 100,000 users within a year.
GitHub raised Series A funding from Andreessen Horowitz at a valuation reportedly around $750 million.
Microsoft acquired GitHub for $7.5 billion in an all-stock deal; Wanstrath became a billionaire as the largest individual shareholder.
Founded Null Games, an independent game publishing studio, after leaving Microsoft.

advantage_archetypes.name: The platform-native builder
advantage_archetypes.description: Grew up with online platforms and direct audience/customer exposure. Built things people used from an early age. Low traditional advantage, high digital-native leverage.

sample_trajectories.event: Moved to Sebastopol, California to work for O'Reilly Media; began blogging on EvHead.com and learning to code.
Co-founded Pyra Labs with Meg Hourihan on January 1; launched Blogger, one of the first blog-publishing platforms.
Pyra Labs and Blogger acquired by Google for an undisclosed sum.
Co-founded Twitter via Obvious Corporation with Jack Dorsey and Biz Stone.
Became CEO of Twitter, succeeding Jack Dorsey.
Founded Medium, an online publishing platform.
Co-founded Obvious Ventures, a venture capital firm focused on world-positive companies.
Stepped down from Twitter board of directors.
Began contributing to the Mozilla open-source project as a computer engineering student at the University of Auckland.
Hired as an intern at Netscape in Mountain View after his Mozilla contributions were noticed by engineer David Hyatt.
Led engineering for Firefox 1.0, the open-source browser that challenged Microsoft's Internet Explorer dominance.
Joined Google to lead user experience for the Chrome browser project.
Joined OpenAI to lead development of the Atlas browser, aiming to challenge Chrome.
Founded MetaMachine and released eDonkey2000, a peer-to-peer file-sharing application that became one of the most popular P2P networks globally.
eDonkey shut down after MetaMachine reached a $30 million settlement with the RIAA over copyright infringement.
Created Mt. Gox, the first major Bitcoin exchange, repurposing a domain originally intended for Magic: The Gathering card trading.
Co-founded Ripple (then OpenCoin) with Chris Larsen and Arthur Britto, serving as CTO and helping architect the XRP Ledger.
Co-founded Stellar, a decentralized payment network designed for fast cross-border transactions, competing with Ripple.
Founded Vast Space, a private aerospace company aiming to build the world's first commercial space station, self-funding the venture with his crypto fortune.
Vast Space preparing to launch Haven-1 commercial space station; Forbes estimated net worth of approximately $3.9 billion.

advantage_archetypes.name: The ordinary-background achiever
advantage_archetypes.description: Few documented early advantages. Achievement came from drive and timing rather than head start.

sample_trajectories.event: Published an early version of the backpropagation algorithm at the COGNITIVA conference in Paris.
Completed PhD in computer science at Universite Pierre et Marie Curie with a thesis on connectionist learning models.
Joined AT&T Bell Labs as a research scientist, where he developed convolutional neural networks (LeNet) for handwriting recognition.
Became head of the Image Processing Research Department at AT&T Labs-Research.
Joined NYU as a professor of computer science at the Courant Institute.
Named Director of AI Research at Facebook (later Meta).
Co-recipient of the ACM Turing Award with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio for work on deep learning.
Co-founded Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs after leaving Meta.
Won silver medal representing Poland at the International Mathematical Olympiad in Vietnam.
Co-authored 'Intriguing properties of neural networks' while at Google Brain, a foundational paper on adversarial examples in neural networks.
Co-founded OpenAI as one of its founding members alongside Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Ilya Sutskever.
Led OpenAI robotics team that created a robotic arm capable of solving a Rubik's Cube.
Continues as co-founder of OpenAI, leading work on GPT models, GitHub Copilot, and Codex.
Won first Italian outdoor title in 200m and was taken under coach Carlo Vittori's guidance
Won Olympic bronze medal in 200m at the Munich Olympics
Won European Championship gold in the 200m
Won European Championship gold in both 100m and 200m in Prague
Set 200m world record of 19.72 seconds at the Universiade in Mexico City
Won Olympic gold medal in 200m at the Moscow Olympics
Died in Rome on March 21, 2013

advantage_archetypes.name: The ordinary-background achiever
advantage_archetypes.description: Few documented early advantages. Achievement came from drive and timing rather than head start.

sample_trajectories.event: Graduated from Tufts University with a degree in computer science; joined Claris, an Apple subsidiary, developing Macintosh software.
Co-founded Ink Development Corp (later eShop Inc.) on May 10, an early online shopping software company.
Launched AuctionWeb (later eBay) on Labor Day weekend as a side project on his personal website.
eShop acquired by Microsoft on June 11; quit his day job at General Magic to focus on eBay full-time.
eBay went public; Omidyar became a billionaire shortly after the IPO.
Founded Omidyar Network, a philanthropic investment firm.
Founded First Look Media, including The Intercept news organization.
Released Drupal 1.0.0 as open-source software on January 15, 2001, from his University of Antwerp dorm project.
Co-founded Acquia with Jay Batson to provide commercial support and services for Drupal.
Named to MIT Technology Review TR35 as one of the top 35 innovators under 35; also named Young Entrepreneurs of Tech by BusinessWeek.
Defended PhD dissertation in computer science at Ghent University on profiling and instrumentation of the JVM.
Acquia helped re-launch Whitehouse.gov on Drupal, cementing Drupal's enterprise credibility.
Acquia acquired by Vista Equity Partners in a deal valuing the company at approximately $1 billion.
Transitioned to Executive Chairman of Acquia as Chris Tranquill was appointed CEO.
Released PHP 1.0 (Personal Home Page Tools) on June 8, 1995, via a Usenet newsgroup announcement.
Contributed to the Apache HTTP Server project and added the LIMIT clause to the mSQL DBMS.
Joined Yahoo! Inc. as an Infrastructure Architecture Engineer, helping migrate Yahoo to PHP-based tools.
Named to MIT Technology Review's list of top innovators for creating PHP, which by then powered over 12 million websites.
Joined Etsy as Distinguished Engineer, working on architecture, internationalization, payments, fraud, and security.

advantage_archetypes.name: The self-made striver
advantage_archetypes.description: Low inherited advantage. Early adversity or constraint acted as a catalyst. Got there through drive, not head start.

sample_trajectories.event: Wrote Gosling Emacs, the first Emacs implementation for Unix in C, while a PhD student at Carnegie Mellon University; it was later commercially distributed by UniPress Software.
Completed PhD in Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University with thesis 'Algebraic Constraints' under Bob Sproull and Raj Reddy.
Led the original design and implementation of the Java programming language at Sun Microsystems, including its compiler and virtual machine.
Elected to the US National Academy of Engineering for the conception and development of Java and contributions to windowing systems.
Briefly joined Google, then became Chief Software Architect at Liquid Robotics, writing software for autonomous ocean-going robots.
Joined Amazon Web Services as Distinguished Engineer, working on IoT projects including AWS Greengrass.
Retired from Amazon Web Services in July 2024 after a career spanning nearly 50 years as a software engineer.
Devised Merkle's Puzzles, an early public-key cryptographic key exchange scheme, as an undergraduate at UC Berkeley.
Submitted the public-key cryptography paper to Communications of the ACM after encouragement from faculty member Bob Fabry.
Joined Diffie and Hellman at Stanford for the summer, becoming part of the public-key cryptography research team.
Completed PhD in Electrical Engineering at Stanford under Martin Hellman with thesis 'Secrecy, Authentication, and Public Key Systems.'
Joined Xerox PARC as a research scientist, where he designed the Khufu and Khafre block ciphers and the Snefru hash function.
Became Distinguished Professor of Computer Science at Georgia Tech before returning to California in 2006.
Received the IEEE Richard W. Hamming Medal jointly with Diffie and Hellman for work on public-key cryptography.
Founded MemoryDealers.com, an online business selling networking equipment that became a market leader generating millions in revenue.
Convicted and sentenced to 10 months in federal prison for selling explosives on eBay.
Discovered Bitcoin and began investing in Bitcoin startups, earning the nickname 'Bitcoin Jesus'.
Renounced US citizenship and acquired citizenship of St. Kitts and Nevis.
Indicted by US federal grand jury for tax evasion related to Bitcoin holdings; arrested in Spain.
Entered deferred prosecution agreement, paying nearly $50 million to settle tax evasion charges.

leverage_archetypes.name: The timed rep-builder
leverage_archetypes.description: Rode a structural wave while putting in serious reps. Not the deepest specialist, but showed up at the right time with enough skill to catch it.

leverage_archetypes.name: The audience-first builder
leverage_archetypes.description: Rode a wave with owned distribution — an audience or platform that compounded. Distribution was the leverage, not skill depth.

leverage_archetypes.name: The relentless practicer
leverage_archetypes.description: Thousands of hours of focused, concentrated practice. Got there through consistency and intensity — reps over timing.

leverage_archetypes.name: The early starter
leverage_archetypes.description: Started serious practice before 20 and accumulated significant reps. Consistency from an early age — the tortoise, not the hare.

leverage_archetypes.name: The early starter
leverage_archetypes.description: Started serious practice before 20 and accumulated significant reps. Consistency from an early age — the tortoise, not the hare.

leverage_archetypes.name: The opportunistic rider
leverage_archetypes.description: Caught a structural wave with enough reps to hang on. Timing was the primary lever — skill was adequate, not exceptional.

leverage_archetypes.name: The moderate lever
leverage_archetypes.description: Moderate leverage across several dimensions. Some reps, some timing, some network — but no dominant built advantage.

leverage_archetypes.name: The rep-accumulator
leverage_archetypes.description: Putting in reps but without a structural wave, deep skill, or strong network to amplify them. Consistency without compounding.
